Configure TMLE Targeting, Positivity Bounds, and Memory Options

Source: R/tmle_spec.R
set_targeting.Rd

Configure TMLE Targeting, Positivity Bounds, and Memory Options

Usage

set_targeting(
  spec,
  cv_tmle = TRUE,
  g_bounds = "adaptive",
  fluctuation = c("logistic", "linear", "none"),
  max_iter = 100L,
  tol = 1e-06,
  save_nuisance = c("predictions", "butcher", "full"),
  parallel = FALSE
)

Arguments

spec

A tmle_spec() object.

cv_tmle

Logical; whether to use Cross-Validated TMLE (out-of-fold nuisance predictions). Strongly recommended (TRUE by default) to preserve valid influence-function standard errors without Donsker assumptions.

g_bounds

Positivity truncation rule for propensity scores: "adaptive" (Gruber & van der Laan \(5 / (\sqrt{n_{\text{eff}}} \ln n_{\text{eff}})\) bounded to [0.01, 0.15]), a single numeric threshold b giving [b, 1 - b], or a length-2 numeric vector c(low, high) in (0, 1).

fluctuation

Fluctuation submodel: "logistic" (bounded canonical logistic fluctuation on scaled [0, 1] outcomes — default), "linear" (weighted linear fluctuation), or "none" (one-step / plug-in without targeting step).

max_iter

Maximum iterative TMLE steps (reserved for iterative updates).

tol

Convergence tolerance on mean EIF.

save_nuisance

Memory policy for nuisance models after fitting: "predictions" (default; keeps only out-of-fold predictions, CV risk, and Super Learner weights for instant retarget() with minimal RAM), "butcher" (strips heavy internals via butcher::butcher()), or "full" (retains full fitted workflows).

parallel

Logical; if TRUE and mirai daemons are active (mirai::daemons_set()), distributes (fold x learner) tasks via mirai::mirai_map().

Value

An updated "tmle_spec" object.

Details

Three built-in statistical guardrails govern the targeting step:

  • CV-TMLE (cv_tmle = TRUE): Uses out-of-fold nuisance predictions so standard errors remain valid even when using non-Donsker machine learning learners such as random forests or boosted trees (Zheng & van der Laan, 2011).

  • Adaptive Positivity Truncation (g_bounds = "adaptive"): Prevents a handful of near-0 or near-1 propensity scores from inflating inverse weights and EIF variance, following the sample-size-aware \(5 / (\sqrt{n}\ln n)\) diagnostic rule (Petersen et al., 2012; Gruber & van der Laan, 2010).

  • Bounded Logistic Fluctuation (fluctuation = "logistic"): Scales continuous outcomes into [0, 1] and performs canonical logistic fluctuation so targeted counterfactual predictions stay strictly inside the observed support even under extreme confounding (Gruber & van der Laan, 2010).

References

Zheng, W., & van der Laan, M. J. (2011). Cross-validated targeted minimum-loss-based estimation. In Targeted Learning (pp. 459–474). Springer.

Gruber, S., & van der Laan, M. J. (2010). A targeted maximum likelihood estimator of a causal effect on a bounded continuous outcome. The International Journal of Biostatistics, 6(1), Article 26.

Petersen, M. L., Porter, K. E., Gruber, S., Wang, Y., & van der Laan, M. J. (2012). Diagnosing and responding to violations in the positivity assumption. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 21(1), 31–54.

Examples

spec <- tmle_spec(y, a, c(age, sex, lab_1)) |>
  set_targeting(cv_tmle = TRUE, g_bounds = c(0.05, 0.95), fluctuation = "logistic")
spec
#> 
#> ── Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation (TMLE) Specification ──
#> 
#> • Outcome: y
#> • Treatment: a
#> • Covariates: c(age, sex, lab_1)
#> • Estimand(s): "ate"
#> • CV-TMLE: TRUE (10-fold)
#> • Positivity bounds: "0.05, 0.95" | Fluctuation: "logistic"
